inventedEvidence.evidence: Borderline only: 'Since you prefer not to check the filter right now' when the customer had said she had not got to it yet and asked for other checks

blockingLoop.evidence: Pump-filter instruction given in turn 2, repeated in full in turn 3 ('Unscrew the pump filter slowly...'), and insisted on again in turn 5 ('we must rule out an airflow blockage first') despite the customer twice asking for other checks; turn 5 offered no next step at all

rationale: The assistant eventually lands on the right direction (heater element or thermal cut-out) and sensibly hands off to an engineer, with correct unplug-first advice. However it wasted most of the conversation pushing the drain pump filter and a user-removable 'condenser' (not relevant to a stone-cold heater on this water-cooled machine), repeating the same step three times while the customer asked for alternatives, and claimed knowledge of 'this model' without ever asking for the full model number. It never asked about an interrupted drying cycle, the key clue in the ground truth, and mischaracterised the customer as preferring not to check the filter. Safe but inefficient and only moderately useful.
